articles.title: An Oregon wheat-farming couple had 13 wind turbines placed on their land; while crops continued around them, they said the operating turbines were bringing in about $100,000 a year
articles.summary: In the dry, rolling hills of Sherman County, Oregon, farming continues alongside huge green energy projects.
articles.body: In the dry, rolling hills of Sherman County, Oregon, farming continues alongside huge green energy projects. For one local wheat-growing family, having wind turbines on their land has changed their yearly finances without stopping their traditional harvest. According to a report by The Oregonian/OregonLive, Kevin McCullough and his wife, Kathryn McCullough, grow wheat on land that contains about half of the Biglow Canyon wind farm. Thirteen of the huge industrial turbines stand directly on their property, turning above fields that are still used to grow crops. The money from the turbines has made a major difference for the family business. It provides a valuable second source of income while the family continues farming. "We were ecstatic," Kathryn McCullough told The Oregonian/OregonLive when talking about the arrival of the turbines. "What's not to like? When these things are turning, we're making $100,000 a year."Dual income on working landThe arrangement shows how rural landowners and energy companies are increasingly working together across North America. Portland General Electric (PGE) opened the Biglow Canyon wind farm 15 years ago as part of a statewide effort to increase renewable energy production. Unlike some energy projects that require large areas to be cleared, wind turbines leave most farmland available for other uses. The concrete bases and access roads cover only a very small part of the total land. That allows farming families like the McCulloughs to keep using combines and planting wheat right up to the bases of the giant towers. Using land for both farming and wind power gives farmers some protection against the changing crop prices and weather problems that come with dryland wheat farming.Safety concerns amidst turbine malfunctionAlthough payments from wind projects can provide steady income, farming next to large energy equipment also brings its own risks and challenges. Safety at the facility came under close attention after a major equipment failure at the Biglow Canyon project. In late January, a delivery driver noticed broken bolts near the base of turbine 71. Just days later, on 1 February, the turbine suffered a serious structural failure. An eight-tonne, 11-story-tall blade was thrown into a nearby wheat field. The spinning blade cut a trench about four feet deep through the crop stubble. The trench was roughly a football field from the turbine base. Heavy mounting bolts were scattered across the surrounding land. The accident immediately raised concerns for farming families working the fields beneath the turbines. After the accident, Kathryn McCullough told The Oregonian/OregonLive about the possible danger to people working nearby. "Someone could have been killed or badly injured," she said. After the blade broke free, PGE took temporary safety steps. The company shut down all 217 turbines at the Biglow Canyon facility. Engineers carried out full inspections and tested the bolts before the turbines were slowly returned to operation.Rural economic backboneDespite the risks shown by equipment failures, payments from wind leases remain an important source of money for landowners in Sherman County and throughout the Columbia River Gorge. Wind projects also bring millions of dollars in local tax revenue in addition to direct lease payments to property owners. That money helps pay for emergency services, public roads, and rural school districts across eastern Oregon. For farming families dealing with uncertain harvests, combining traditional farming with yearly turbine payments provides a steady source of income. That predictable money can help families keep their agricultural land financially sustainable from one generation to the next.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Residents sceptical of temporary fixes
articles.summary: Madurai residents doubt monsoon readiness as many areas rely on temporary flood fixes like desilting and pumps, while permanent KfW drainage works cover only key sites.
articles.body: Madurai: While Madurai corporation has taken up permanent storm water drainage overhaul at key locations under KfW funding, residents across the city’s remaining vulnerable locations remain highly sceptical about monsoon preparedness.Residents in severely affected localities, including Sellur, Vandiyur, Ayyan Pappakudi, and Old Ramnad Road, are still dependent on short-term fixes. The civic body continues to rely on temporary interventions, such as drain desilting, mobile pumps, mini-excavators, and robotic machinery to tackle recurrent waterlogging during the rainy season.Root-cause analysis reveals that nearly half the city’s waterlogging issues stem from structural blockage, followed by low-lying plots, overflowing water bodies, insufficient drain cross-sections, non-availability of drains, and seepage from nearby PWD channels.“Repeated attempts at desilting the water channels are very temporary solutions to a long-standing issue. Every year, the issue of flooding crops up when it rains. The entire sewage system needs to be overhauled completely and modernised to account for the increased population in the city,” said VP Manikandan, a social activist living in SS Colony in Madurai.A senior corporation official said that plans are in place to revamp the entire sewage system in the city. “We are focusing on the most heavily used areas first, while the remaining parts of the city will be given attention in the next year,” the official said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Madurai | Silver Rate in Madurai | Bank Holidays in Madurai | Public Holidays in Madurai | Madurai AQI | Weather in Madurai | Petrol Price in Madurai | Diesel Price in Madurai | CNG Price in Madurai | LPG Price in MaduraiStay updated with the latest Madurai news. articles.title: Rowdy arrested for vandalising police booth, assaulting cops
articles.summary: Trichy police arrested history-sheeter M Mohammed Saleem for vandalising a police beat box and assaulting cops; booked under BNS sections and TN property damage act.
articles.body: Trichy: A 43-year-old history-sheeter was arrested in Trichy on Thursday on charges of vandalising a police booth and shoving police officials.Police said M Mohammed Saleem lives at Alwarthoppu near Thillai Nagar in Trichy. He is listed as a known depredator (KD).Police said two special police sub-inspectors were on duty near the beat box at Alwarthoppu around 5pm when Saleem, who was under the influence of alcohol, came there. When the officers questioned him, Mohammed Saleem argued with them. He then forced open the beat box, went inside and damaged the glass of a window and a couple of chairs, police said. During the incident, Saleem verbally abused the officers, pushed them to the ground, and issued threats.Thillai Nagar police registered a case against him under sections 329(4), 296(b), 132, 131, and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), for trespassing, public nuisance, assault, assault on a public servant, and criminal intimidation. articles.title: NMC urges commercial establishments to offer free toilet access to women
articles.summary: Nashik Municipal Corporation urges malls, hotels, restaurants and petrol pumps to offer women free toilet access, with hygiene, water, lighting and signage.
articles.body: Nashik: To improve access to sanitation facilities for women across the city, the Nashik Municipal Corporation (NMC) administration has appealed to shopping malls, multiplexes, hotels, restaurants, petrol pumps and other commercial establishments to allow women to use their toilet facilities free of charge.Nashik municipal commissioner Manisha Khatri has urged all commercial establishments not to charge any fee for use of toilets by women and voluntarily support the initiative, which aims to ensure easy access to safe and clean toilets for women and girls travelling for work, education, shopping or any other activities in Nashik.The civic administration has requested establishments to maintain hygiene at the facilities, adequate water supply and proper lighting for women’s comfort while using the facilities. Commercial establishments have been asked to sensitise their staff and extend full cooperation to women and display signboards indicating that toilet facilities are available free of cost for women.Women often face difficulties in locating toilets while travelling within the city, particularly in busy commercial areas. The initiative intends to bridge this gap by utilising existing infrastructure available at commercial establishments and making Nashik a more women-friendly city.An NMC official said easy access to sanitation facilities remains an important aspect of creating a safe and inclusive urban environment, adding that the initiative supplements the existing public toilet network and is expected to improve convenience for women travelling long distances.The NMC operates a network of public sanitation facilities across the city. There are 466 public and community toilets with over 6,000 seats in Nashik. Of these, around 183 are public toilets in key public places, while 283 are community toilets in slum areas and residential localities.Community toilets are primarily used by local residents, whereas public toilets cater to commuters and visitors and are managed by private agencies appointed by the municipal corporation.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Nashik | Silver Rate in Nashik | Bank Holidays in Nashik | Public Holidays in Nashik | Petrol Price in Nashik | Diesel Price in Nashik | CNG Price in Nashik | LPG Price in NashikStay updated with the latest Nashik news. articles.body:
A member of the defensive ranks at La Liga giants Barcelona currently boasts the best pass accuracy of any player in Europe's top-5 leagues in 2026/27.

The Blaugrana star in question? Andreas Christensen.

Stopper Christensen is for his part currently condemned to a fresh spell on the sidelines, owing to a muscular problem suffered during a La Liga meeting with Sevilla last month.

Prior to as much, though, the Danish international had been afforded a prominent role by boss Hansi Flick, to the tune of six league appearances, four of which came in the form of starts.

And as alluded to above, along the way, Christensen's exploits in one area in particular proved to be of nothing short of a world-class level.

'Andreas Christensen has a better pass accuracy (97.4%) than any other player in Europe's top five leagues this season (200+ mins).'
